fields.display_title: This paper studies the LS-SVM MTL method in multi-task learning in the large-p large-n setting. By utilizing mathematical tools in random matrix theory, it characterizes the asymptotic behavior of the classification score and thus proposes to choose the decision threshold and training labels in an optimal way. The theory matches the simulation results well, and the competency of the proposed method is demonstrated via synthetic and real data analysis.

Replying to This paper studies the LS-SVM MTL method in multi-task learning in the large-p large-n setting. By utilizing mathematical tools in random matrix theory, it characterizes the asymptotic behavior of the classification score and thus proposes to choose the decision threshold and training labels in an optimal way. The theory matches the simulation results well, and the competency of the proposed method is demonstrated via synthetic and real data analysis.

fields.display_title: The paper introduces the random matrix theory to study the performance of MTL LS-SVM theoretically, which is novel. Meanwhile, The theoretical analysis is based on MTL LS-SVM with data from a Gaussian mixture model, which limits the generality of the work.

Replying to The paper introduces the random matrix theory to study the performance of MTL LS-SVM theoretically, which is novel. Meanwhile, The theoretical analysis is based on MTL LS-SVM with data from a Gaussian mixture model, which limits the generality of the work.

fields.display_title: The paper provides interesting theoretical insights in multi-task learning using common and specific parameters modeling framework and based on least-squares SVM. Especially, it is theoretically established that the standard MTL LS-SVM is biased. Thereon a method derived from the analysis is proposed to correct the bias and allows to achieve enhanced performances. Empirical evaluations highlight the effectiveness of the method.
